rest.payment.answers.bodyUnreadable: Any endpoint that takes a body (`POST /api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/topup`, `POST /api/v1/payment/gateway/midtrans/notifications`), when the body is missing, is not JSON, has anything after the JSON value, or holds a value of the wrong type, including a `paymentMethod` or `bank` that is not one of the listed names. Fields the endpoint does not know are ignored. Nothing was recorded; correct the body before sending it again.
rest.payment.answers.tokenRefused: Any endpoint that needs a token, when payment does not accept what Kong let through: no `Authorization: Bearer` header reached payment, or the token is not an access token (a refresh token or a sign-in challenge token carries identity's signature too, and passes Kong), its `aud` lacks the audience payment expects, its issuer is not identity, it has expired, or payment cannot find its signing key in identity's key set. A `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge comes with the answer. Get a new access token from identity and retry; right after identity rotates its keys, payment fetches them again at most once every 10 seconds, so a retry after that can succeed.
rest.payment.answers.claimMissing: Any wallet endpoint, when the token passes every check but its `sub`, `email` or `role` claim is missing, empty or not a string. `error` names the claim. Identity puts all three in every access token it issues; sign in again.
rest.payment.answers.noRoute: Any path under `/api/v1/payment` that names no endpoint, with a token Kong and payment accept. `error` repeats the path without its leading slash. A trailing slash is not ignored: `/api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/balance/` is a different path.
rest.payment.answers.methodNotAllowed: Any endpoint, when the path exists but not with this method, and the token is accepted: for example `DELETE` on a balance, or `GET` on `/api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/topup`. `Allow` lists the methods the path takes.
rest.payment.answers.mediaType: Any endpoint that takes a body, when a body is sent with no `Content-Type`, or with one that is not JSON. `Accept` lists the types the endpoint reads; send `Content-Type: application/json`.
rest.payment.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that payment did not expect. Whether the request took effect is unknown: read the current state (the balance, or the top-up by its `referenceNumber`) before acting again. A top-up retried with the same `Idempotency-Key` is never charged twice.
rest.payment.answers.database: Any endpoint, when payment cannot get a connection to its database within 3 seconds, or the database fails in a way that may pass. Retry later; a top-up retried with the same `Idempotency-Key` is never charged twice.
rest.payment.answers.signingKeys: Any endpoint that needs a token, when payment cannot read identity's signing keys (identity does not answer within 5 seconds, cannot be reached, or sends a key set payment cannot read), so it cannot tell whether the token is valid. Nothing was done; retry later.
rest.payment.customerBalance.summary: Reads the caller's customer wallet: the balance that can be spent at checkout. Reading never creates the wallet.
rest.payment.customerBalance.who: Customers only (`role` `customer`). The wallet is always the caller's own, the one of the token's `sub`; every other role, `admin` included, gets `403`.
rest.payment.customerBalance.case.found: The wallet exists. Amounts are rupiah with two decimals; a top-up is never accepted or credited when it would take the balance above IDR 2,000,000. `heldOrPendingBalance` is always `0.00` for a customer: no payment flow holds back part of a customer's balance.
rest.payment.customerBalance.case.notYet: No money has reached a customer wallet for the caller yet. The answer is a wallet at zero with `id` `null` and `exists` `false`; nothing is stored until money first reaches it.
rest.payment.customerBalance.case.wrongR: The caller's `role` is not `customer`. `error` names the caller's role.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.summary: Starts a top-up of the caller's customer wallet through Midtrans, by bank virtual account or QRIS, and answers with how to pay. The balance does not change here: it changes once Midtrans reports the payment and payment has confirmed it with Midtrans.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.who: Customers only (`role` `customer`), always into their own wallet; every other role, `admin` included, gets `403`.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.field.idempot: 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`. Names one top-up for good, per caller: the same key with the same body answers with that top-up again instead of charging a second time, and the same key with a different `amount`, `paymentMethod` or `bank` is refused. Make a new key for each top-up the customer starts, and send the same one on every retry of it.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.field.amount: Whole rupiah, from 1,000 to 2,000,000; a fraction is refused, because Midtrans charges whole rupiah. The wallet's balance plus `amount` must also stay within the IDR 2,000,000 a customer wallet may hold, which is checked before Midtrans is called.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.field.payment: `MIDTRANS_VA` (bank virtual account) or `MIDTRANS_QRIS`, in capitals as written.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.field.bank: Required with `MIDTRANS_VA`, refused with `MIDTRANS_QRIS`. One of `BCA`, `BNI`, `BRI`, `CIMB`, `PERMATA`.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.charged: Midtrans created the charge. Keep `referenceNumber` and show `instructions`: the virtual account to pay into (`qrCodeUrl` instead for QRIS) and `expiresAt`, Midtrans' deadline as Midtrans writes it. `status` stays `PENDING` and the balance is unchanged until the payment settles; read the outcome with `GET /api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/topup/{referenceNumber}`. `instructions` is `null` if Midtrans' answer named neither a virtual account nor a QR code.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.replayed: This `Idempotency-Key` was used before with the same `amount`, `paymentMethod` and `bank`. Nothing is charged again: the answer is that top-up as it stands now, so `status` may already be `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED` or `NEEDS_ATTENTION`, and `instructions` is there only while it is `PENDING`.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.missingK: The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing. Nothing was recorded.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.invalid: The body breaks an annotated rule: `amount` missing or below 1,000, or `paymentMethod` missing. `error` lists every broken rule, sorted and joined by `; `. Nothing was recorded.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.ruleBrok: The request breaks a rule payment checks itself: an `Idempotency-Key` outside its characters or length, an `amount` with a fraction, no `bank` with `MIDTRANS_VA` or a `bank` with `MIDTRANS_QRIS`, or a `paymentMethod` other than those two. `error` names the rule. Nothing was recorded.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.wrongRol: The caller's `role` is not `customer`. `error` names the caller's role.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.keyReuse: The caller already used this `Idempotency-Key` for a top-up with a different `amount`, `paymentMethod` or `bank`. Nothing was charged; a new top-up needs a new key.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.amountAb: `amount` is above the largest single top-up, IDR 2,000,000. `code` is `TOP_UP_AMOUNT_ABOVE_LIMIT`, and `limit` is that maximum in whole rupiah, as a string. Nothing was recorded.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.walletFu: The wallet's balance plus `amount` would be above the IDR 2,000,000 a customer wallet may hold: here a wallet at IDR 1,650,000 asked for IDR 500,000. `code` is `WALLET_BALANCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and `limit` is the most the wallet may hold, as a string. Nothing was recorded and Midtrans was not called.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.gatewayR: Midtrans refused the charge. The top-up is recorded as `FAILED` under `referenceNumber`: no charge exists and no balance changed. Every retry with this key gets the same answer; start again with a new key.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.gatewayU: Midtrans gave no definite answer: it did not answer within 15 seconds, could not be reached, or answered with a server error or with something payment cannot read. The top-up stays `PENDING` under `referenceNumber`, and the charge may exist. Do not start another top-up: read this one with `GET /api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/topup/{referenceNumber}`. If the customer did pay, Midtrans' notification settles it; failing that, payment's own sweep asks Midtrans about top-ups pending longer than 10 minutes, every 5 minutes by default.
rest.payment.customerTopUp.case.earlierA: An earlier request with this `Idempotency-Key` got no definite answer from Midtrans, or is still waiting for one. Nothing is charged again; read the top-up with `GET /api/v1/payment/wallet/customer/topup/{referenceNumber}` instead of retrying.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.summary: Reads one of the caller's own top-ups: its status, and how to pay while it is pending. It shows what payment has recorded and does not ask Midtrans.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.who: Customers only (`role` `customer`), for their own top-ups; every other role gets `403`.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.field.r: The `referenceNumber` from the top-up's answer: `TOPUP-` followed by a UUID.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.case.pe: The top-up waits for the customer's payment. `instructions` is read again from Midtrans' answer to the charge, as in the top-up's first answer; it is `null` while that answer is still unknown.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.case.co: The top-up is concluded, and `instructions` is `null`. `SUCCESS`: the amount was credited to the wallet, once. `FAILED` or `EXPIRED`: nothing was credited. `NEEDS_ATTENTION`: what Midtrans reported does not let payment credit the wallet on its own, so a person resolves it; nothing has been credited.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.case.wr: The caller's `role` is not `customer`. `error` names the caller's role.
rest.payment.customerTopUpStatus.case.no: No top-up with this reference belongs to the caller: it does not exist, or it is another customer's. Both are answered alike.
rest.payment.merchantBalance.summary: Reads the caller's merchant wallet: what has been released to the seller, and what is still held for orders not yet completed. Reading never creates the wallet.
rest.payment.merchantBalance.who: Sellers only (`role` `seller`). The wallet is always the caller's own; every other role, `admin` included, gets `403`.
rest.payment.merchantBalance.case.found: The wallet exists. `availableBalance` is money released to the seller; `heldOrPendingBalance` is the seller's share of orders that are paid but not completed, released when each order is completed. Amounts are rupiah with two decimals; a merchant wallet has no upper limit.
rest.payment.merchantBalance.case.notYet: No money has reached a merchant wallet for the caller yet. The answer is a wallet at zero with `id` `null` and `exists` `false`; nothing is stored by reading.
rest.payment.merchantBalance.case.wrongR: The caller's `role` is not `seller`. `error` names the caller's role.
rest.payment.driverBalance.summary: Reads the caller's driver wallet: delivery fees already released to the courier, and fees still held. Reading never creates the wallet.
rest.payment.driverBalance.who: Couriers only (`role` `courier`). The wallet is always the caller's own; every other role, `admin` included, gets `403`.
rest.payment.driverBalance.case.found: The wallet exists. `availableBalance` is delivery fees released to the courier; `heldOrPendingBalance` is fees held for deliveries not yet settled. Amounts are rupiah with two decimals; a driver wallet has no upper limit.
rest.payment.driverBalance.case.notYet: No money has reached a driver wallet for the caller yet. The answer is a wallet at zero with `id` `null` and `exists` `false`; nothing is stored by reading.
rest.payment.driverBalance.case.wrongRol: The caller's `role` is not `courier`. `error` names the caller's role.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.summar: Receives Midtrans' payment notifications for top-ups. A notification is only a prompt: payment then asks Midtrans for the transaction's status and acts on that answer, never on the notification's own `transaction_status`.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.who: Midtrans. No token: Kong lets `POST` to this exact path through without one, and payment authenticates the notification by its `signature_key` instead.
The top-up's `referenceNumber`, which payment sent to Midtrans as the order id.
Midtrans' status code, as a string. Part of the signature.

The amount as Midtrans writes it, a string with two decimals. Part of the signature. It is not what gets credited: payment credits the amount it recorded, and only when Midtrans' status answer settles exactly that amount.

The SHA-512 of `order_id`, `status_code`, `gross_amount` and the server key payment shares with Midtrans, concatenated in that order, as hex in either case. Compared in constant time. If any of the four fields is missing or empty, the notification is refused.
Read and ignored: payment asks Midtrans for the status itself.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.case.p: The signature verifies and the top-up is known. `status` is the top-up's status after payment asked Midtrans: `SUCCESS` when the payment settled and the wallet was credited, `PENDING` when Midtrans has not settled it yet, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, or `NEEDS_ATTENTION` when it cannot be credited on its own. A notification for a top-up already concluded changes nothing and answers its status, so a repeated notification never credits twice.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.case.s: `signature_key` does not verify, or one of `order_id`, `status_code`, `gross_amount` and `signature_key` is missing or empty. Nothing was read or changed.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.case.u: The signature verifies, but no top-up is recorded under `order_id`.
rest.payment.midtransNotification.case.g: Payment could not get a usable status from Midtrans: no answer within 15 seconds, unreachable, a server error, or a status it cannot act on. Nothing was decided and the top-up stays `PENDING`. A later notification settles it; failing that, payment's own sweep asks Midtrans about top-ups pending longer than 10 minutes, every 5 minutes by default.
